lesson_title: In a Line or Side by Side
hook_text: Three identical resistors. Put them in a line and the lamp dims. Put them side by side and it brightens. Here is why, and how to draw both.
clip_script: A resistor is a striped tube built to resist; read it digit, digit, zeros: brown black brown is 100 ohms. Series, in a line: resistances add, 100 plus 100 is 200, current falls, lamp dims, volts shared out. Parallel, side by side: more doors out of the hall, total resistance drops below the smallest, two 100s act like 50, current rises, lamp brightens, full volts on each branch. Draw series as rectangles end to end, one path, no dots. Draw parallel stacked between two lines, a dot at every junction. Build both, bet on the brighter lamp first.
visual_style: Whiteboard resistor with colour bands decoding; three rectangles in a row with a dimming lamp; three stacked between rails with dots and a brightening lamp; a hall with one door, then two.
pacing: Resistor and code, series, parallel, the two drawings.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and decode three resistors from your kit.
